text.p: Alliance Entertainment Corp on Thursday said it has put in implemented a consolidation plan to cut costs and to increase margins.

The firm said that it would reduce its domestic warehouses from eight to three and cut its workforce by up to 20 percent, resulting in expected annual cost savings of approximately $20 to $22 million once the plan is completed.
Alliance expects to take a charge in the 1996 fourth quarter of about $28 to $32 million as a result of the changes. The plan is expected to be completed by March of 1998.

Al Teller, Alliance co-chairman and chief executive, said in a statement, "I believe that the completion of this plan will significantly enhance the company's competitive position within the music industry."

"As part of the refocusing of the company's operations, Alliance is also considering divesting itself of its Brazilian operations and its artist management operation, Teller added. "Depending on the results of this evaluation, such divestitures might result in additional charges with respect to such operations."
Alliance distributes pre-recorded music and music-related products.
